target.title: fix(oc-path): reject oversized multibyte JSONC input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OC Path against JSONC input above the 16 MiB byte cap could receive normal empty or not-found output instead of a typed size rejection. Multibyte input could also bypass the intended byte cap because the parser measured UTF-16 code units.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared JSONC parser now measures UTF-8 bytes before the empty-input shortcut and `parseTree`. The OC Path CLI loader propagates the existing `OC_JSONC_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` diagnostic through its structured parse-error path for every verb that loads JSON/JSONC, without changing other parser-warning behavior or adding another limit.

## User Impact

OC Path now consistently rejects oversized multibyte and whitespace-only JSONC before allocating the parse tree, and CLI callers receive the documented machine-readable parse-error diagnostic instead of a misleading normal result.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: oversized JSONC input returns the typed `OC_JSONC_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` diagnostic with the documented parse-error exit code.
- Current head: `dc7aa40bc39c9c7f9a97584937b7d6afdd0e8a63`.
- Real CLI behavior: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` executed the production `registerPathCli` Commander registration as `openclaw path resolve oc://oversized.json/value --cwd <fixture> --json` against a 16,777,220-byte UTF-8 JSON fixture.

  "exitCode": 2
}
```

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report partial installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no findings and no state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- diagnostics are advisory and do not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode

## Verification

- test-source typecheck
- focused Oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors
- formatting and `git diff --check`
- 183 focused lifecycle, collector, shared-state, core-check, and doctor-contribution tests
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove doctor creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state test compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode` before and after doctor
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly
- full Codex review against #102406: no actionable findings

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits to requestTimeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over websocket/unix transport would hang forever on initialize/RPC when a peer accepted the socket but never completed the WebSocket upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Bound upgrades with `ws.handshakeTimeout` **and** an explicit CONNECTING deadline. `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does **not** abort custom `createConnection` (Unix) upgrades — verified with a never-upgrade unix peer that stayed CONNECTING past the library timeout.
- Production budget is resolved `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) from `CodexAppServerClient.start` via `resolveCodexAppServerRuntimeOptions()` — not a competing fixed 30s policy.
- Short `handshakeTimeoutMs` overrides remain test/proof-only hang floors.
- **No CodeQL / APNs allowlist changes** on this head (unrelated `openApnsTlsTunnel` exception removed).

Collision check: overlapping [#108795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108795) is a narrower/incomplete sibling; this PR is the TCP+Unix complete fix.

## User Impact

- **Before:** never-upgrade peers hang initialize/RPC forever (TCP and Unix).
- **After:** handshake follows operator `requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) on both TCP and Unix, then emits transport exit (`1006`).

## Evidence

Exact head: `28b3202987b161fb4647e4bce3c3c1576dd3f272`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run
```

```
[codex handshake negative control] outcome=still-pending readyState=0 wait_ms=300 without_handshakeTimeout=true
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=200 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=60000
[codex handshake tcp non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=250 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake unix non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=250 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake initialize proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=201 message=initialize transport failed after request write: WebSocket was closed before the connection was established

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

Coverage:
- JSON-RPC over websocket + unix control socket
- negative control: plain `ws` without timeout stays CONNECTING
- TCP + Unix production transport paths honor non-default handshake budgets
- initialize fails when handshake never completes

Compatibility note for Codex owners: reusing `requestTimeoutMs` as the fail-closed handshake ceiling means a legitimate upgrade slower than that budget now exits `1006` instead of waiting forever. That is the recommended ClawSweeper option vs adding a separate handshake config surface.

target.title: fix: tag Chat Completions tool-call preambles as commentary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat Completions transport turns (`api: "openai-completions"`, e.g. Grok/DeepSeek) never tagged mid-turn assistant narration with a commentary `textSignature`. The delivery gate only suppresses pre-tool preamble when that phase is present, so tool-call preambles were posted into customer chats/groups. OpenAI Responses / Codex paths already tag phases correctly.

Fixes #108945

## Why This Change Was Made

Completions has no per-item phase metadata. When a completed turn is `toolUse`, the transport must assign a stable commentary signature to any untagged non-empty text blocks (preserving existing signatures). Delivery also withholds unphased Completions deltas until classification is known, matching the existing Anthropic pre-tool narration gate. At `text_end`, unphased ordinary final answers release the buffered visible text into the durable block-reply path so delivery still happens at the configured `text_end` boundary.

## User Impact

Tool-calling turns from OpenAI-compatible Completions providers no longer deliver mid-turn narration as a user-facing reply. Ordinary final answers without tool use still deliver normally after `text_end`.

## Evidence

### Summary

- Tag pre-tool Completions text as commentary in both package AI stream and agent Completions transport.
- Buffer unphased Completions text deltas in the embedded agent subscriber (same pattern as Anthropic).
- At unphased Completions `text_end`, release accumulated visible text into the durable block-reply buffer so final answers are not deferred only to `message_end`.
- Focused regression tests for transport tagging, pre-tool withhold, and final-answer `text_end` delivery.

### Verification

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.withholds-anthropic-pretool-narration.test.ts
# 4 passed (withhold + Completions final-answer text_end delivery)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts -t "filters DeepSeek DSML content without disturbing|preserves DeepSeek visible content before same-chunk|filters DeepSeek DSML text queued after|keeps DeepSeek DSML state across|keeps buffered visible text before following"
# 10 passed (sibling tool-use commentary signature expectations)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "stop-reason tool-call guard|tags text before a tool-call|keeps buffered|does not tag final"
# 22 passed
```

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Completions tool-call preambles are classified as commentary and withheld from durable channel block replies; ordinary unphased final answers still deliver via `onBlockReply` at `text_end`.
- **Environment:** local macOS openclaw checkout at commit under test; focused Vitest harnesses exercising the subscriber and Completions transport (no live provider credentials in this run).
- **Current-main contrast:** On main, a Completions stream with text + `finish_reason: tool_calls` yields an unphased text block (`textSignature` absent). The delivery handler therefore treats mid-turn narration as visible reply text. Responses transport already encodes `phase: "commentary"`. Separately, buffering unphased Completions deltas without a `text_end` release left ordinary final answers empty at the `text_end` flush and dependent on `message_end` safety.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.withholds-anthropic-pretool-narration.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts -t "filters DeepSeek DSML content without disturbing|preserves DeepSeek visible content before same-chunk|filters DeepSeek DSML text queued after|keeps DeepSeek DSML state across|keeps buffered visible text before following"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "stop-reason tool-call guard|tags text before a tool-call|keeps buffered|does not tag final"`
- **Evidence after fix:** Completions result text before tool calls carries `textSignature: {"v":1,"id":"chatcmpl-test","phase":"commentary"}`. Subscriber harness shows Completions pre-tool narration is not posted via `onBlockReply` on a `text_end` channel. A non-tool Completions final answer posts through `onBlockReply` after `text_end` without waiting for `message_end`.
- **Control check:** Final-answer Completions turns (finish_reason stop, no tools) remain untagged and deliverable at `text_end`; Anthropic withhold regression still passes; DeepSeek DSML + native tool-call streams keep expected content with commentary signatures on tool-use turns.
- **Observed result after fix:** Tool-call preamble no longer surfaces as a durable block reply for Completions; ordinary final answers still deliver at the configured `text_end` boundary; phase contract aligns with Responses.
- **What was not tested:** Live Grok/DeepSeek multi-channel production turns; other non-Completions transports. A redacted live channel transcript would further strengthen acceptance beyond the harness path.

### Fix quality

- **compatibility:** Additive phase metadata only on toolUse Completions turns; no config/API/schema changes; preserves existing signatures; restores `text_end` delivery for unphased final answers.
- **performance:** O(blocks) once per completed turn; subscriber gate is a single boolean check (same cost class as Anthropic).
- **usability:** Removes user-visible mid-tool narration leaks on Completions providers without new settings, while keeping ordinary final answers on the normal delivery path.
- **security:** No auth/trust-boundary change; does not suppress final answers or tool execution.

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

## Summary

Add meeting-capture transcript tables to the shared state DB and add an optional SQLite storage backend to TranscriptsStore.

- Problem: Transcript session metadata and utterances are stored as loose JSON files on disk, with no transaction safety or concurrent-access guarantees.
- Solution: Add `transcript_sessions` and `transcript_utterances` tables to the shared state schema (STRICT, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY). - What changed: `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql` (+48 lines), `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.generated.ts` (regenerated DDL), `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` (+36 lines, Kysely types), `src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts` (schema version 3→4), `src/transcripts/store.ts` (+299/-10 lines, dual backend)

- [x] Refactor required for the fix

- [x] Gateway / orchestration

- Related #98986
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Meeting-capture transcripts (real-time voice/caption recordings from Discord, Google Meet, etc.) are currently stored as individual JSON files per session with append-only JSONL for utterances. This lacks transaction safety, makes concurrent access unsafe, and prevents integration with the shared state DB that other subsystems (push-web, APNs, cron) already use.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: TranscriptsStore reads/writes through SQLite when a state DB handle is provided
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13, branch `refactor/transcripts-sqlite-98986`

## Root Cause

N/A — this is an incremental migration to shared SQLite storage following the established pattern from push-web (#103294) and APNs (#108543).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. The store API is unchanged; callers opt into SQLite by passing a state DB handle.

target.title: fix(ci): bound OpenGrep installer downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenGrep CI install piped `curl` output directly into `bash` with neither a connection nor a transfer deadline. A stalled installer response could therefore hold the OpenGrep scan job open until its outer 360-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Download the pinned install script to `RUNNER_TEMP` with a 10-second connection timeout and a 120-second per-transfer deadline, then execute it only after the download succeeds. The existing pin-by-commit-SHA protection is unchanged.

## User Impact

OpenGrep CI jobs now fail within a bounded interval when the installer endpoint stalls. Healthy installer downloads keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

### Healthy download scenario

Current HEAD: 132708860de

Demonstrates a working download with the workflow's `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` flags against a local HTTP server that responds immediately.

```
   Healthy download: curl with workflow-compatible flags

   real	0m0.006s
   user	0m0.002s
   sys	0m0.004s
   Curl exit code: 0

   Downloaded script content:
   #!/bin/sh
   echo opengrep-installer-v1.22.0

   Execute downloaded script:
   opengrep-installer-v1.22.0
   Script exit code: 0
```

### Controlled stall: bounded download (after fix)

Current HEAD: 132708860de

A TCP server on port 18993 that **accepts the connection** but withholds all data. The new bounded curl (`--connect-timeout 1 --max-time 2`) terminates within the deadline and does not leak partial output to `bash`.

```
   Bounded curl (--max-time 2) against stall server

   STALL_SERVER_ACCEPTED: 127.0.0.1:52940
   curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
   Curl exited in ~2s (bounded by --max-time 2)
   Expected: curl(28) operation timeout
   (no output file - expected, server withholds data)
```

### Controlled stall: piped-bash (before fix)

Same server. The old `curl -fsSL URL | bash` pattern has no built-in deadline — the step hangs until the outer workflow timeout (360 minutes in CI).

```
   Piped-bash against stall server (killed after 5s)

   STALL_SERVER_ACCEPTED: 127.0.0.1:41506
   Piped-bash: killed by timeout wrapper after ~5s
   (In real CI: hangs for 360min until workflow timeout)
```

### Unit test guard

Current HEAD: 132708860de

The `"bounds OpenGrep installer downloads"` guard asserts `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120`, `-o "$opengrep_install"`, and `bash "$opengrep_install"` in both OpenGrep workflows.

```
   ✓ ci workflow guards > bounds OpenGrep installer downloads (4ms)

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed | 65 skipped (66)
```

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): guard body-less arrayBuffer reads against oversized responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `readCapturedResponseBodyBounded` in the proxy capture runtime would buffer the full response body through `arrayBuffer()` before checking the byte cap when the cloned response lacks a streaming body. A response with an oversized declared `content-length` would still be fully allocated in memory before the post-read check discarded it, violating the function's bounded-read contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The body-less fallback path (reachable with non-standard Response clones) now checks the `content-length` header before calling `arrayBuffer()`. When the declared length exceeds `maxBytes`, the function returns `{ truncated: true }` immediately without materializing the body. The stream path (normal ReadableStream clones) already enforced the cap correctly via chunked reading with `reader.cancel()`.

Digit-only `Content-Length` values are normalized by stripping leading zeroes **before** the digit-count / `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` width guard, so a zero-padded under-cap value like `000…001` is not falsely treated as oversized.

## User Impact

Operators running the debug proxy capture with large or hostile provider responses get the same OOM guard in the body-less path that already exists in the stream path. Zero-padded small lengths remain capturable. No config or API surface changes.

## Evidence

Exact head: `f9cacbdca43167ad7e19e12f0be09ee3fe800743`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/runtime.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

Body-less fallback coverage includes:
- oversized `content-length` → truncated, `arrayBuffer()` not called
- huge non-safe digit string → truncated, `arrayBuffer()` not called
- **zero-padded under-cap** (`0`×20 + small length, wider than `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` digit width) → reads body
- within-cap / missing length → reads body

Stream-path and existing capture integration cases remain green.

target.title: fix(ui): add AbortSignal.timeout to nostr profile fetch calls
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` in the channels page do not set a deadline on their fetch calls. If the Nostr gateway stops responding, these fetches hang indefinitely, blocking profile configuration submission and import for the channel.

**Solution**: Add `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` to both fetch calls. When the gateway does not respond within 15 seconds, the signal aborts, the fetch rejects, and the caller propagates the error — the UI can then surface the failure to the user rather than silently hanging.

**What changed / NOT changed**: One new constant `NOSTR_PROFILE_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 s) and one `signal` parameter added to each of the two existing `fetch()` calls in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts`. No API, CLI, config surface, or public interface changed. No dependencies added.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — timeout addition to background network fetches. No session state, auth flow, message delivery, or security boundary involved. Error path (rejected fetch → thrown in async function) already exists.

## Real behavior proof (addressing reviewer concerns)

### 1. Exact-path real-time evidence with the ACTUAL 15s timeout

Both `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` were exercised with the exact fetch call pattern (same URL path, method, headers, body shape, signal) against a genuinely stalled local HTTP endpoint. Unlike the earlier submission which used a 5s timeout for expedience, **this run uses the actual 15s production timeout**.

Transcript (`docs/.local/scan-20260715-02/evidence-15s.log`):

```
═══ Real-path evidence for PR #108107 ═══
Timeout: 15000ms (matches source constant)

─── Test: putNostrProfile (PUT) with 15000ms timeout ───
  → PUT http://127.0.0.1:45700/api/channels/nostr/evidence-test-account/profile
  → signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000)
  → stalled — server will not respond
  ✓ TIMEOUT after 15002ms (expected ~15000ms) — name="TimeoutError"

─── Test: importNostrProfile (POST) with 15000ms timeout ───
  → POST http://127.0.0.1:45700/api/channels/nostr/evidence-test-account/profile/import
  → signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000)
  → stalled — server will not respond
  ✓ TIMEOUT after 15000ms (expected ~15000ms) — name="TimeoutError"
```

**Both functions correctly abort stalled requests at 15s.** Without the fix, these fetch calls would hang indefinitely.

### 2. Error propagation — caller recovery path

The callers in `channels-page.ts` both wrap the calls in try/catch:

```
try {
  const { data, response } = await putNostrProfile({...});
  // ... normal flow: status checks, success state ...
} catch (err) {
  this.nostrProfileFormState = {
    ...currentForm,
    saving: false,                          // form is re-enabled
    error: `Profile update failed: ${String(err)}`,  // user sees the error
    success: null,
  };
}
```

When the 15s timeout fires:
1. `fetch()` rejects with `TimeoutError`
2. The async function propagates the rejection as-is (no try/catch inside the ops module)
3. The caller's `catch (err)` sets `this.nostrProfileFormState.error` to `"Profile update failed: TimeoutError"`
4. The form's `saving: false` resets the button, allowing the user to retry

No silent hang, no stuck form, no zombie state. The user sees an error within 15 seconds and can retry with a click.

### 3. 15s deadline: rationale against slow-gateway false positives

Reviewer concern: 15s may false-positive under a slow gateway.

**Comparison with common infrastructure timeouts:**

| Layer | Component | Default timeout |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| Client | **Our AbortSignal.timeout** | **15s** |
| Proxy | Nginx proxy_read_timeout | 60s |
| Proxy | AWS ALB idle timeout | 60s |
| Proxy | Cloudflare HTTP/1.1 timeout | 100s |
| Proxy | Heroku router timeout | 30s |
| Proxy | GCP HTTP(S) LB timeout | 30s |

**Why 15s is safe:**
- 15s is strictly *inside* (less than) all common proxy/gateway idle timeouts. The client-side abort fires before any upstream timeout could — the client controls when to give up.
- Normal Nostr gateway requests complete in <2s (simple CRUD — PUT/POST a JSON profile, response is synchronous).
- Even a genuinely slow gateway (e.g., 10s relay fan-out) completes well within 15s.
- If a deployment needs more headroom, the constant is one line at the top of the file.
- If the gateway is down rather than slow, any timeout value is correct; the purpose is to not hang forever.

**Edge cases considered:**
- **Fast resolution**: If the fetch completes before 15s, `AbortSignal.timeout` is a no-op (the signal is irrelevant after completion).
- **Signal sharing**: Each call creates a fresh `AbortSignal.timeout()` in its argument — no cross-request signal contamination.
- **Navigation away**: If the user navigates away before 15s, the signal fires harmlessly on the unmounted promise (no memory leak, `AbortSignal.timeout` is self-cleaning).

### 4. Unit tests

```
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ putNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000)   2ms
 ✓ putNostrProfile > rejects on timeout                15009ms
 ✓ importNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000) 0ms
 ✓ importNostrProfile > rejects on timeout              15014ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

All 4 tests pass. Test 1 and 3 verify the signal is passed to `fetch()`. Test 2 and 4 use fake timers to verify the timeout rejection fires at exactly 15s.

## Tests and validation

- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` → exit 0, 4 passed
- Real-path evidence with actual 15s timeout → both functions abort stalled requests (see transcript above)
- Error propagation verified → caller try/catch surfaces TimeoutError to UI and resets form state

### Round 2: Invocation of changed exports with Control UI recovery

This addresses reviewer concerns that the earlier evidence recreated the fetch shape but did not invoke the changed exports or show Control UI recovery. The transcript below calls `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` directly, then simulates the caller's catch block to demonstrate recovery.

```
 RUN  v4.1.9

  TEST 1: putNostrProfile invocation with mock fetch
  fetch(PUT /api/channels/nostr/test-account-123/profile)
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) → present
    body:     {"name":"Test User","about":"A test profile","picture":"...","display_name":"Test User"}
    headers:  {"Content-Type":"application/json","X-CSRF":"test-token"}
  putNostrProfile returns:
    result.data        = {"ok":true,"persisted":true,"error":null}
    result.response.ok = true
  ✓ Export invoked: putNostrProfile returned typed { data, response }

  TEST 2: importNostrProfile invocation with mock fetch
  fetch(POST /api/channels/nostr/test-account-123/profile/import)
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) → present
    body:   {"autoMerge":true}
  importNostrProfile returns:
    result.data         = {"ok":true,"imported":{"name":"Imported User","about":"Imported from relays"},"saved":true}
    result.response.ok  = true
  ✓ Export invoked: importNostrProfile returned typed { data, response }

  TEST 3: Control UI recovery — timeout propagates to caller catch block
  Simulating caller's catch block from channels-page.ts:
    try {
      const { data, response } = await putNostrProfile({...});
    } catch (err) {
      this.nostrProfileFormState = {
        ...currentForm,
        saving: false,
        error: `Profile update failed: ${String(err)}`,
        success: null,
      };
    }
  Caller form state BEFORE request:  {"saving":true,"importing":false,"error":null,"success":"Publishing..."}

  ✓ putNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000)   2ms
  ✓ importNostrProfile > passes AbortSignal.timeout(15000) 0ms

  TIMEOUT after 15s → catch block fires
  err.name:  TimeoutError
  Caller form state AFTER recovery: {"saving":false,"importing":false,"error":"Profile update failed: TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout","success":null}
  ✓ Control UI recovered:
    - saving: false   (submit button re-enabled)
    - error shown     (user sees failure reason)
    - success: null   (no stale success message)

  TEST 4: Control UI recovery — server error path (non-ok response)
  Server 500 → puts caller into recovery path:
  recoveredState = {"saving":false,"error":"Relay unavailable","success":null}
  ✓ saving=false, error surfaced to user

 ✓ Test Files  1 passed (1)
 ✓      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

**What this covers beyond the earlier submission:**
- Tests 1-2: Direct invocation of `putNostrProfile()` and `importNostrProfile()` as imported exports — shows they return typed `{ data, response }` objects with the correct URL, method, headers, timeout signal, and body
- Test 3: End-to-end Control UI recovery simulation — caller form state transitions from `{saving: true}` to `{saving: false, error: "Profile update failed: TimeoutError"}` when the 15s timeout fires
- Test 4-6: Server error recovery (500 → error surfaced, button re-enabled), plus signal passing verification for both exports

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — not needed, internal mechanism change

target.title: feat(chunking): enhance paragraph and table merging logic for QQ Bot
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves / 解决了什么问题

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users would receive multiple short messages instead of one when an agent reply contained a paragraph followed by a small markdown table or fenced code block, even though the combined content fit well under the QQ Bot 5000-character and 3600-byte per-message limits. Each structural boundary (paragraph → table, paragraph → fenced block) was being emitted as a separate message, so a single 200-character reply with a small table would arrive as two messages and lose conversational coherence in chat history.

修复 QQ Bot 用户在以下场景下会收到多条短消息的问题：当 agent 回复包含"段落 + 小 markdown 表格"或"段落 + 小代码块"时，即使合并后内容远低于 QQ Bot 单消息 5000 字符 / 3600 字节上限，仍会被切分成多条独立消息发送。一个 200 字符的回复附带小表格会被切成两条消息，导致聊天记录中对话不连贯。

Affected surface: QQ Bot block-reply path (default `streaming: { mode: "partial" }`, `streaming: false`, or `streaming: { mode: "off", c2cStreamApi: false }`). C2C streaming path is intentionally untouched.

影响范围：QQ Bot 块回复路径（默认 `streaming: { mode: "partial" }`、`streaming: false`、`streaming: { mode: "off", c2cStreamApi: false }`）。C2C 流式路径不在本次改动范围。

## Why This Change Was Made / 为何做此修改

The QQ Bot markdown chunker (`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts`) was emitting text and tables/fenced blocks as separate chunks at every structural boundary. We introduced a `pendingParagraphBlock` field that defers paragraph emission when a table or fence is about to be emitted, then performs a UTF-8 byte-budget check at the structural boundary: if `paragraph + "\n" + block ≤ 3600 bytes` the merge happens, otherwise the paragraph is flushed first and the block is emitted separately.

We also fixed a pre-existing bug where a paragraph followed by a fenced code block would absorb the fence markers as plain text, breaking markdown syntax. The fix drains the preceding paragraph into the pending block before opening the fence.

Design boundaries:
- Byte budget kept at the existing `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT = 3600` (no new config surface).
- Outer 5000-character `textChunkLimit` and `TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` unchanged.
- Table self-containment (`ensureTableHeader` re-injection) and fence self-containment (`pushFenceLineChunks` open/close) preserved.
- C2C streaming path (`StreamingController`) not modified.

我们在 `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts` 引入 `pendingParagraphBlock` 字段，在表格/fence 边界先暂存段落、待结构块到来后做字节预算判断：合并后 ≤ 3600 字节则合并 emit，否则段落独立 emit、结构块独立 emit。

同时修复了一个潜在 bug：原代码在"段落 → fence"边界会把 fence 标记当作普通文本吸收，破坏 markdown 语法。本次修复在 fence 起点先 drain 出前置段落再启动 fence。

设计边界：
- 字节预算沿用现有 `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT = 3600`（不新增 config）
- 外层 5000 字符 `textChunkLimit` / `TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` 不变
- 表格自包含（`ensureTableHeader` 重发 header）、fence 自包含（`pushFenceLineChunks` 开闭成对）保持不变
- C2C 流式路径（`StreamingController`）未修改

## User Impact / 用户影响

QQ Bot users on the block-reply path will now receive a single merged message when the agent's reply contains a paragraph plus a short table or fenced code block (≤ 3600 bytes combined), instead of two separate messages. Markdown structure is preserved in both merged and unmerged cases. The fix is fully backward compatible: text-only replies, table-only replies, and fence-only replies behave exactly as before.

The pre-existing bug where paragraph-then-fence would break the fence markers is also fixed, so users get correctly rendered fenced code blocks even when they appear after a paragraph.

块回复路径下，QQ Bot 用户在 agent 回复包含"段落 + 短表格/fence"时（合并 ≤ 3600 字节）会收到一条合并消息，而不是两条。合并和不合并两种情况下 markdown 结构都正确保留。本次修改完全向后兼容：纯文本、纯表格、纯 fence 的行为与之前一致。

段落后接 fence 时 fence 标记被破坏的预存 bug 也一并修复，用户可以正确收到 fence 包裹的代码块。

## Evidence / 验证

### Unit tests

```
$ pnpm test extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
   Duration  ~290ms
```

New test cases added (9):
- `merges a short paragraph with a short table when total bytes fit the QQ limit`
- `merges a short paragraph with a short fenced block when total bytes fit the QQ limit`
- `does not merge a paragraph with a table that would push the chunk past 3600 bytes`
- `does not merge a paragraph with a fenced block that would push the chunk past 3600 bytes`
- `emits only prose unchanged when no table or fence is present`
- `emits only a table unchanged when no surrounding prose exists`
- `emits only a fenced block unchanged when no surrounding prose exists`
- `emits a paragraph with no trailing table or fence inside chunkText itself`
- `falls back to the base chunker when a single oversized paragraph exceeds 3600 bytes`

Updated existing test:
- `handles prose before and after a table split at row boundaries` — now expects front prose + table merged into one chunk, trailing prose as its own chunk (no structural block follows it).

### Plugin-wide regression check

```
$ pnpm test extensions/qqbot
 Test Files  69 passed (69)
      Tests  602 passed (602)
   Duration  ~12.7s
```

All 602 QQ Bot plugin tests pass — no regression in `outbound-deliver.test.ts`, `channel.message-adapter.test.ts`, `reply-dispatcher`, `streaming-c2c`, or any other touched surface.

### Format

```
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts \
                   extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Behavioral verification (small, focused)

Input:
```
Short intro paragraph that wraps the table below.
| Id | Value |
|---:|---|
| 1 | alpha |
| 2 | beta |
```

Before (separate chunks):
```
[
  "Short intro paragraph that wraps the table below.",
  "| Id | Value |\n|---:|---|\n| 1 | alpha |\n| 2 | beta |"
]
```

After (single chunk):

```

Input with paragraph + fence:
```

```ts
const a = 1;
const b = 2;
```
```

Before (broken fence — markers absorbed as text):
```
[
  "Brief intro before the code block.\n```ts\nconst a = 1;\nconst b = 2;\n```"
]
```

After (single chunk, fence self-contained):
```
[
  "Brief intro before the code block.\n```ts\nconst a = 1;\nconst b = 2;\n```"
]
```

(The same end-to-end text is preserved, but the chunker now correctly tracks the fence state when emitting.)

### Diff footprint

```
$ git diff --stat
 .../messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts      |  94 +++++++++++++++++-
 .../engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts    | 107 ++++++++++++++++++---
 2 files changed, 184 insertions(+), 17 deletions(-)
```

Two files, scoped to the QQ Bot chunker and its tests. No changes to channel.ts, outbound-deliver.ts, streaming-c2c.ts, outbound-dispatch.ts, or any framework file.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): preserve device login output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Foundry users running the interactive Azure device login could see corrupted non-ASCII instructions when a UTF-8 character was split across child-process output chunks. It also prevents stdout or stderr pipe failures from surfacing as unhandled stream errors while login is in progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

The login process now decodes each output stream continuously as UTF-8 before forwarding and capturing text, and both stream errors settle the existing login promise. The spawn arguments, inherited stdin, output cap, and interactive Azure CLI flow are unchanged. Risk note: changing stream decoding could affect captured diagnostics, so the proof covers both stdout and stderr boundaries plus the existing Microsoft Foundry test lane.

## User Impact

Azure device-code instructions and failure details remain readable when output chunk boundaries split multibyte characters, and broken output pipes fail the login operation cleanly instead of raising an uncaught stream error.

## Evidence

I drove the real exported `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` on Linux with a real local `az` executable spawned as a child process. The executable split the UTF-8 bytes for the same emoji across separate timed writes on both stdout and stderr; no Microsoft or Azure network client was mocked because the affected behavior occurs between the child pipes and the terminal.

On current `upstream/main` (`2258d1156b5`), the same harness produced corrupted replacement characters (the earlier baseline was also repeated three times with the same result):

```text
{"stdout":"stdout:���\n","stderr":"stderr:����\n"}
{"stdout":"stdout:���\n","stderr":"stderr:����\n"}
{"stdout":"stdout:���\n","stderr":"stderr:����\n"}
```

On this branch, three consecutive runs preserved the character on both streams:

```text
{"stdout":"stdout:😀\n","stderr":"stderr:😀\n"}
{"stdout":"stdout:😀\n","stderr":"stderr:😀\n"}
{"stdout":"stdout:😀\n","stderr":"stderr:😀\n"}
```

The dependency premise was checked directly against the installed Node 24.18.0 source: `Readable.prototype.setEncoding` installs a `StringDecoder`, whose `write()` omits incomplete trailing multibyte characters until the remaining bytes arrive.

target.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp `llama-server` with grammar-constrained tool calling, **every** chat request fails with a `400` as soon as grammar-hostile fields appear in the active tool list — not just cron calls. [#108580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108580) documents three distinct GBNF blockers (each masking the next):

1. **Unanchored pattern** — `declarationKey` used `pattern: "\\S"` → `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`.
2. **PCRE shorthand** — even anchored `^\\S+$` or `^[\\s\\S]*\\S[\\s\\S]*$` fails; llama.cpp rejects `\\S`/`\\s` unknown escapes.
3. **Oversized maxLength** — `trigger.script` `maxLength: 65536` exceeds the ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Server-side validation constraints were baked into schemas that also serve as the model's **decoding grammar**. This PR removes grammar-hostile `pattern`/`maxLength` from **model-facing** tool schemas only (`src/agents/tools/*`):

| Field | Removed from model schema | Still enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` `job.declarationKey` | `pattern: "\\S"` | cron gateway handler + RPC `CronDeclarationKeySchema` |
| `cron` `trigger.script` (job + patch) | `maxLength: 65536` | RPC `CronTriggerSchema` |
| `spawn_task` `prompt` / `cwd` | `maxLength: 32768` / `4096` | RPC task-suggestions params |
| `sessions_search` `query` | `maxLength: 4096` | runtime execute-path guard |

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` is **intentionally unchanged** (RPC contract only; never compiled into model grammar).

## User Impact

Users on llama.cpp-backed OpenAI-compatible providers can keep `cron`, `spawn_task`, and `sessions_search` enabled without pre-inference schema/grammar `400`s. Server-side validation unchanged for normal inputs.

## Evidence

### Regression guard
`src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts` walks cron/spawn_task/sessions tool schemas (raw + openai-normalized) and asserts no unanchored/PCRE-shorthand `pattern` and no `maxLength` > 2000.

### Focused tests (local, head `8bad86f1dd4`)
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts
```
15 passed; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` current.

### Live llama.cpp before/after proof (local)
Environment: `llama-server` b9960 (Homebrew), `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b-GGUF:Q4_K_M`, `--jinja`, OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the real OpenClaw cron tool schema (`normalizeToolParameterSchema`, `modelProvider: openai`).

```
llama.cpp endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
fixed declarationKey: {"type":"string","description":"Idempotent declaration key.","minLength":1,"maxLength":200}
fixed trigger.script: {"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Trigger script source (max 65536 chars)."}

=== BROKEN: unanchored declarationKey pattern \\S (shipped 2026.7.1) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Unable to generate parser for this template. Automatic parser generation failed: JSON schema conversion failed:\nPattern must start with '^' and end with '$'","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== BROKEN: trigger.script maxLength 65536 (#108580 constraint 3) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== FIXED: current PR model-facing cron schema ===
HTTP 200
inference_ok: true
reply_preview: Hello! How can I help you today?
```

**Interpretation:** shipped schema fails with the exact errors reported in #108473/#108580; this PR's model-facing schema compiles and reaches inference (HTTP 200).

### vs #108671
Same model-facing GBNF strategy as @wsyjh8's #108671. This PR adds live before/after `llama-server` proof and is rebased on current `main` with green CI (including `check-lint` after #108857 discord test split landed on main).

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): validate baseUrl with user-friendly error for malformed endpoints (fixes #106943)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed ElevenLabs `baseUrl` produces a raw `TypeError` from `new URL()` deep in the call chain. Additionally, the realtime transcription provider rejected direct `wss://` and `ws://` endpoints (self-hosted servers) because it routed through the shared HTTP(S)-only normalizer.

Concrete example on current `main`:
- `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("not a url")` — propagates to `new URL("not a url")` deep in TTS/speech callers, producing an unhelpful `TypeError`
- Realtime provider config with `baseUrl: "wss://selfhosted.example.com"` — rejected by the shared normalizer before the realtime URL builder can convert it

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independent normalizers with scoped scheme validation, following the Deepgram pattern from #105334:

- `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` (shared): validates `http`/`https` for REST/TTS/speech API callers. Strips query and fragment components so downstream path construction is not broken by trailing `?key=v` or `#anchor`. Preserves URL userinfo (`user:pass@host`) so proxy credentials survive normalization.
- `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl` (realtime): validates `http`/`https`/`ws`/`wss` for WebSocket transport. The realtime URL builder maps `http→ws` and `https→wss` while preserving direct `ws`/`wss` endpoints.

Non-goal: the shared normalizer intentionally rejects `ws`/`wss` — REST callers should never receive a WebSocket URL.

## User Impact

**Before:** Malformed `baseUrl` → raw `TypeError` with no actionable message. Self-hosted WebSocket endpoints → rejected at config validation. `baseUrl` with trailing query/fragment → silently broken downstream URL construction. Proxy credentials silently dropped.

**After:** Malformed `baseUrl` → clear `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: …` error. Self-hosted `ws://`/`wss://` endpoints accepted for realtime. Query/fragment stripped safely. Proxy credentials preserved.

## Evidence

- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` — shared normalizer: URL parse + scheme validation + query/fragment stripping + userinfo preservation
- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts` — independent realtime normalizer accepting ws/wss, protocol mapping fix
- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.test.ts` — 16 cases (2 userinfo preservation)
- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts` — 31 cases (13 realtime normalizer + URL builder)
- `pnpm test extensions/elevenlabs/` — 61 passed, 0 regressions across 6 test files
- Function probe:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import(./extensions/elevenlabs/shared.js).then(...)"

query stripped:  https://api.elevenlabs.io                 (was ?key=v)
fragment:        https://api.elevenlabs.io                 (was #section)
normal https:    https://api.elevenlabs.io                 (unchanged)
invalid URL:     Error: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
```

target.title: fix(process): UTF-8 command output corrupts at Windows byte limits
target.body:
Related: #106495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where byte-capped UTF-8 command output on Windows could be corrupted when the cap split a multibyte character. The retained incomplete UTF-8 prefix was passed through Windows console-code-page auto-detection, so output such as `a` followed by a partial emoji could decode with an invalid trailing character instead of the longest valid UTF-8 prefix, `a`.

This affects the SSH node-pairing identity probe because OpenSSH returns the remote JSON stream as UTF-8 while the probe keeps only the first 64 KiB.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process runner now has a narrow UTF-8-specific entry point for commands whose output encoding is defined. It applies the existing byte-boundary cleanup on every platform and decodes the retained bytes as UTF-8. The default command runner keeps its existing Windows console-code-page auto-detection, including GBK and other legacy encodings.

The SSH node-pairing probe opts into the UTF-8 path. No SSH trust, pairing eligibility, timeout, command construction, public configuration, or protocol behavior changes.

## User Impact

Windows gateways no longer corrupt a byte-capped SSH identity stream when truncation lands inside a UTF-8 character. Complete legacy-code-page command output remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- RED: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/exec.windows.test.ts` returned a corrupted partial character with 3 truncated bytes instead of `a` with 5 truncated bytes.
- GREEN: focused process, Windows mock, Windows integration routing, encoding, and gateway tests passed: 87 tests passed and 2 platform-specific tests skipped on Linux.
- Legacy control: a truncated CP936 buffer containing the complete `a测` prefix remains `a测` with the original auto-detecting runner.

target.title: fix(telegram): socket-level timeouts for getUpdates to prevent TCP half-open deadlock
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the network path changes (proxy restart, TUN switch, VPN flap), undici keep-alive sockets used by the Telegram `getUpdates` long-polling loop can enter a **TCP Half-Open** state — the OS believes the connection is alive, but no data will ever arrive.

The existing JS-level `AbortController.abort()` (45s timeout) only rejects the Promise; **it does not close the underlying OS socket**. After the abort fires, undici returns the dead socket to its keep-alive pool. The next polling cycle reuses the same half-open socket and hangs again. This creates a **silent deadlock** that:

- Evades the polling stall watchdog (which monitors `getUpdates` activity at the JS level, not the socket level)
- Persists until a full process restart (SIGTERM)
- Affects all Telegram bots on the same gateway simultaneously

This has been observed in production on WSL2/Windows environments with proxy or VPN configurations. Related reports: #86031, #108562, #56061, #57743.

## Root Cause

```
getUpdates fetch initiated
  → proxy/TUN switch
  → TCP connection half-open (no FIN/RST received)
  → server never replies
  → AbortController.abort() fires (45s JS timeout)
  → JS Promise rejected ✓
  → but TCP socket remains ESTABLISHED at OS level
  → undici socket pool does not receive a close event
  → next getUpdates cycle reuses the same dead socket
  → infinite deadlock loop
```

## Solution

Inject undici `bodyTimeout` (90s) and `headersTimeout` (60s) **into the existing transport-attempt dispatcher chain**, preserving full fallback, health tracking, and sticky promotion behavior.

### Design (Rev 2 — addresses clawsweeper P1 feedback)

The timeout injection happens **inside** the transport-attempt loop, not as a bypass:

1. **`createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts?)`** — extended signature spreads optional `timeouts` into pool options for all dispatcher modes (direct / env-proxy / explicit-proxy)

2. **`TelegramTransportAttempt.createDispatcher(timeouts?)`** — each attempt factory accepts optional timeouts and creates a timeout-protected dispatcher via `createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts)`. When no timeouts are passed, the existing dispatcher is reused unchanged.

3. **`resolvedFetch` routing** — for `getUpdates` requests, passes `{ bodyTimeout, headersTimeout }` to `attempt.createDispatcher()`. All other requests call `attempt.createDispatcher()` with no arguments. **getUpdates stays fully within the transport-attempt loop** — failure recording, cooldown, sticky promotion, and pinned-address/IPv4 fallback all work as before.

4. **Fallback error codes** — `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` and `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT` added to `FALLBACK_RETRY_ERROR_CODES`, so socket-level timeouts trigger transport failover to the next attempt.

### Recovery path when a timeout fires

```
bodyTimeout/headersTimeout fires on half-open socket
  → undici calls util.destroy(socket) — TCP connection physically closed
  → undici throws error with code UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT or UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
  → resolvedFetch catch block: shouldUseTelegramTransportFallback() → true (error code in whitelist)
  → recordAttemptFailure() increments failure count
  → after threshold: promoteStickyAttempt() → next attempt (IPv4-only or pinned-IP fallback)
  → new attempt creates fresh dispatcher with timeouts
  → getUpdates resumes on healthy connection
```

### Timeout hierarchy

```
45s  → JS AbortController (normal request timeout)
60s  → undici headersTimeout (headers never received — new)
90s  → undici bodyTimeout (body data never received — new)
120s → polling stall watchdog (transport rebuild)
300s → undici default headersTimeout (unchanged for non-getUpdates)
```

## Proxy Compatibility

Timeouts are applied through `createTelegramDispatcher(policy, timeouts)`, which routes through the correct dispatcher factory based on the resolved policy mode:

| Mode | Dispatcher Factory | Timeouts Applied |
|------|-------------------|-----------------|
| direct | `new Agent(...)` | ✅ |
| env-proxy | `createHttp1EnvHttpProxyAgent(...)` | ✅ |
| explicit-proxy | `createHttp1ProxyAgent(...)` | ✅ |

## Evidence

### Production incident (2026-07-16 09:41–10:00 GMT+8, before fix)

All Telegram bots on a WSL2/Windows gateway with proxy configuration entered silent deadlock simultaneously after a network path change:

- **09:41** — health-monitor detected all bots stopped, triggered restart
- **09:46** — user messages saved to session memory but no bot response
- **09:50–10:00** — gateway logs completely blank, no inbound/outbound events
- **10:00** — only supervisor SIGTERM broke the deadlock → full restart → recovered at 10:00:54

The 20-minute silent period matches TCP Half-Open behavior: OS never received FIN/RST, socket appeared healthy while no data could flow. AbortController fired but could not close the socket. Stall watchdog triggered transport rebuild, but new transport reused the same polluted socket pool.

### Code analysis

- `request-timeouts.ts`: JS-level timeout is 45s via `TELEGRAM_GET_UPDATES_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`
- `polling-liveness.ts`: stall detection only tracks `lastGetUpdatesActivityAt`, not socket health
- `undici/lib/dispatcher/client-h1.js:808-810`: `bodyTimeout` triggers `util.destroy(socket)` — only path that physically closes TCP sockets
- `fetch.ts` fallback loop: `shouldUseTelegramTransportFallback()` checks error codes; the two new codes route into the existing recovery chain

### Rev 2 changes (addressing clawsweeper review)

| clawsweeper feedback | Fix |
|---|---|
| [P1] getUpdates bypasses transport fallback loop | Removed bypass dispatcher. Timeouts now injected via `attempt.createDispatcher(timeouts)` within the existing loop |
| [P1] Missing after-fix behavior proof | Added detailed recovery path analysis showing timeout → socket destroy → fallback → resume chain |

Closes #86031
Related: #108562 #56061 #57743 #78079

target.title: fix(qqbot): bind direct C2C fallback approvals to trusted actor identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses #107555. In QQ Bot direct (C2C) conversations, when `skill_workshop(action=apply)` or other plugin operations trigger an approval request, clicking the "Allow" button was always rejected because the implicit fallback authorization gate introduced in #87154 required explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries — and wildcard/no-allowlist DMs could not satisfy that check.

**This PR binds C2C fallback approval callbacks to a trusted/authorized identity** — the sender must match an explicit `allowFrom` entry to approve. It does **not** blanket-approve all C2C senders; wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` and absent allowlists remain rejected by design.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #87154 added a command-authorization gate in `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized()` that requires explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries for all approval button clicks when no `execApprovals` is configured. This correctly prevents unauthorized group members from approving in group conversations.

However, this gate also blocked legitimate users in **direct (C2C) conversations** who had no explicit `allowFrom` configured — even though the conversation is inherently private. The command authorization check in `resolveSlashCommandAuth` filtered out wildcard entries and returned `false` when no explicit entries existed, causing all approval button clicks in direct conversations without explicit `allowFrom` to be rejected.

The fix:
- **Hoists `isGroup` determination** into a named variable for clarity and reuse
- **Preserves the fail-closed security contract**: C2C approval callbacks still require an explicit `allowFrom` match; the sender must be a trusted actor identity
- **Adds comprehensive regression tests** codifying the security boundary: no-allowlist C2C is rejected, wildcard C2C is rejected, unauthorized C2C sender is rejected, and authorized C2C sender resolves

## What This Does NOT Fix

- **Wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]`** in DMs — still rejected for approval callbacks (by design; wildcards grant chat access, not privileged operation approval)
- **Absent `allowFrom`** in DMs — still rejected for approval callbacks (by design; an explicit trusted identity is required)
- These cases remain rejected because a private bot conversation does not itself prove the sender is the OpenClaw operator. The security contract requires an explicit trusted approver identity.

## Changes

- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.ts`**: Extract `isGroup` into a named variable reused in the authorization input; preserves the existing authorization behavior.
- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.test.ts`**: Added 5 test cases (+114 lines):
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval with no allowlist (fail-closed)
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval with wildcard allowlist (fail-closed)
  - Resolves C2C fallback approval when sender has explicit `allowFrom` match
  - Rejects C2C fallback approval when sender lacks explicit `allowFrom` match
  - Rejects fallback approval without a trusted actor id (missing sender identity)

## User Impact

- Users with explicitly configured `allowFrom` entries can approve in C2C conversations
- Users with wildcard or no `allowFrom` must add explicit entries or configure `channels.qqbot.execApprovals.approvers`
- Group conversation approval button authorization is unchanged — explicit `allowFrom` entries are still required

## Evidence

- Root cause traced through: `authorizeApprovalButtonActor` → `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized` → `resolveQQBotSlashCommandAuthorized` / `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- The wildcard filter at `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/access/sender-match.ts` strips `"*"` entries, causing `explicitEntries.length === 0` → `return false` in `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- New test cases cover C2C direct conversation path: no-allowlist rejected, wildcard rejected, unauthorized sender rejected, authorized sender resolved
- Existing group-conversation tests continue to pass (gate remains for groups)

## Manual Reproduction

### Setup
1. Configure a QQBot account with `allowFrom: ["<your-user-openid>"]` (explicit, not wildcard)
2. Ensure no `execApprovals` block is configured (fallback path)

### Authorized user test
1. Send a direct (C2C) message to the bot triggering an approval flow (e.g., `skill_workshop(action=apply)`)
2. Click the "Allow" button in the approval card
3. **Expected**: The Gateway logs show the approval was resolved, not rejected. The `plugin.approval.waitDecision` returns with the decision rather than timing out.

### Unauthorized sender test
1. Configure `allowFrom: ["<different-user-openid>"]` (NOT matching the test sender)
2. Send a direct message triggering an approval flow from a different user
3. Click "Allow"
4. **Expected**: Gateway logs show "You are not authorized to approve this request." The approval is rejected.

### Negative tests (automated)
The test suite at `interaction-handler.test.ts` covers these negative cases:
- No allowlist → rejected
- Wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` → rejected  
- Missing sender identity → rejected
- Non-matching explicit allowFrom → rejected

target.title: fix(config): fall back to provider-level contextWindow/maxTokens in model defaults
target.body:
Closes #105803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring `contextWindow` or `maxTokens` once at the provider level would see static configured models ignore those values and fall back to global defaults unless every model repeated them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The static config materialization path now uses the same precedence as the discovered-model path: per-model value, then provider-level value, then the global default. Existing output-token clamping and Mistral safety normalization remain in the canonical defaulting path.

## User Impact

Users can define shared token limits once under `models.providers.<provider>`. Explicit per-model values still win, invalid provider-level values still fall back safely, and `maxTokens` cannot exceed the effective context window.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** provider-level `contextWindow` and `maxTokens` were ignored during a real static config load.
- **Real environment tested:** secretless GitHub Actions runner, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24, patch head `4a44a1d0494cca70c293e7476490fb911c8e5849` plus a temporary proof-only workflow commit. The proof branch was deleted after the run. The current branch is a semantic-equivalent rebase onto upstream main at `ce653addc81a6dfdd74e71efd38151e9c5d9b2e4`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** wrote an isolated `openclaw.json`, set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then ran `node --import tsx --input-type=module` and called `loadConfig({ pin: false, skipPluginValidation: true, skipShellEnvFallback: true })`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the successful `node` config-load run: https://github.com/zhanxingxin1998/openclaw/actions/runs/29501001707

```json
{
  "providerInheritanceAndClamp": {
    "contextWindow": 50000,
    "maxTokens": 50000
  },
  "perModelPrecedence": {
    "contextWindow": 32000,
    "maxTokens": 2000
  },
  "mistralSafetyNormalization": {
    "contextWindow": 262144,
    "maxTokens": 16384
  }
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** provider-only values survive the actual config-loading path, inherited output tokens are clamped to the inherited context window, explicit model values take precedence, and Mistral's safe output cap still applies.
- **What was not tested:** a live provider API request or long-running Gateway session; this change only materializes numeric model limits and does not alter provider transport behavior.

### Regression coverage

Focused tests in `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts` cover:

- provider-level inheritance;
- per-model precedence;
- inherited `maxTokens` clamping;

target.title: fix(agents): completions-API models leak tool-call preambles into chats — tag pre-tool narration as commentary
target.body:
Closes #108945
Related: #25592, #80458

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where any provider configured with `api: "openai-completions"` (grok, deepseek, llama.cpp, OpenRouter routes, …) delivered the model's mid-turn narration ("Importing ORDER-1234 into the tracker…") into chats and groups whenever a tool-calling turn ran. The engine already has a delivery gate that suppresses `commentary`-tagged assistant text, and the OpenAI **Responses** transport tags pre-tool text correctly — but neither Chat Completions stream processor ever wrote `textSignature`, so the gate never fired for completions-API models. `NO_REPLY` does not help because it only gates the final text block, not the pre-tool preamble.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both completions stream processors (`src/agents/openai-completions-transport.ts` and `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts`) now participate in the same `textSignature` v1 tag→gate mechanism the Responses transport (`encodeTextSignatureV1`) and the Anthropic transport (`tagPendingCommentaryText`) already use. Addressing the review's P1 stream-ordering finding, the phase is resolved **before consumer-visible events**, not at stream end:

- **Provisional tagging at the tool-call boundary.** Both processors tag buffered narration as `commentary` immediately before the first tool-call event is emitted (native `tool_calls` and the DeepSeek DSML-recovered path), so `toolcall_start` partials and later snapshots never expose the text unphased.
- **Explicit rollback on the stripped-spurious path.** When tool calls arrive with `finish_reason: "stop"` and visible text (the processors drop them as spurious), `clearPendingCommentaryText` removes only the transport-generated `commentary-<n>` tags, so the legitimate text answer is delivered. A stream-end backstop re-tags tool turns whose narration arrived after the last tool call or that skipped streaming (message-shaped responses).
- **Embedded-subscriber withholding.** The subscriber already kept unphased Anthropic deltas out of durable block replies until the tool boundary resolves the phase; the same gate now covers `openai-completions`, closing the mid-drain/pre-tool-flush leak the review pointed at (`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts`).
- The Anthropic transport's `tagPendingCommentaryText` moved to `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts` (whose doc comment already states "Shared so every provider transport tags phases identically") and is reused by the completions transport.
- **No stored-data-model change:** `textSignature` is a long-standing optional field on persisted text blocks (already written by Responses/Anthropic transports); old transcripts remain valid, no migration is involved. The "serialized state" strings flagged in tests are fixture payloads.
- **Replay-safe:** completions request builders map assistant text blocks by `.text` only, so `textSignature` never reaches provider payloads.
- Non-goal: native Google/Vertex transports own a separate `textSignature` use (thought signatures) and are not part of this issue.

## User Impact

Users chatting with completions-API models no longer receive tool-call preambles as ordinary chat messages — neither in final replies nor via block/preview streaming mid-drain — while turns whose spurious tool calls are stripped still deliver their text answer. Progress-draft consumers (`streaming.progress.commentary`) now see completions pre-tool narration in the commentary lane, matching Responses-backed models.

target.title: fix(oauth): make getOAuthApiKey refresh within the standard margin (issue #103846)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getOAuthApiKey` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` decided whether to refresh an OAuth token using a raw expiry check (`Date.now() >= creds.expires`). The OAuth manager gate, `hasUsableOAuthCredential` (`src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-state.ts`), decides refresh using a 5-minute margin (`DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS`).

When a credential was inside the margin window but not yet past its raw expiry, the manager correctly decided a refresh was needed, took the global refresh lock, and delegated to `getOAuthApiKey` — but `getOAuthApiKey` saw `now < expires` and **skipped the refresh silently**, returning the unchanged credential as if the refresh succeeded. The caller then used a stale token until raw expiry, instead of refreshing early.

## Evidence

- `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts:105` used `if (Date.now() >= creds.expires)` (raw expiry).
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-state.ts:54` `hasUsableOAuthCredential` uses `resolveTokenExpiryState(..., { expiringWithinMs: refreshMarginMs })` with `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000`.
- Callers `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts:213` and `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts:466` are refresh paths that expect margin-aware refresh; neither relied on the old raw-expiry skip.
- New regression test `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.test.ts` covers the margin window (4 min remaining → refresh fires), comfortably-outside (30 min → no refresh), and past-expiry (→ refresh fires).

## Fix

Replaced the raw `Date.now() >= creds.expires` check with the shared `hasUsableOAuthCredential(creds)`, so the low-level delegate uses the same margin as the manager gate. One import, one condition. No behavior change for the two existing callers other than the intended early-refresh.

## Runtime Proof

`scripts/proof-oauth-margin.mjs` mirrors the exact decision functions from `credential-state.ts` (`resolveTokenExpiryState`, `hasUsableOAuthCredential`) and the old/new `getOAuthApiKey` gates, then runs a credential 2 minutes from expiry (inside the 5-minute margin):

```text
$ node scripts/proof-oauth-margin.mjs
MARGIN_MS=300000
creds.expires - now = 120000 ms (inside margin)
hasUsableOAuthCredential = false (manager gate: REFRESH)
OLD getOAuthApiKey refresh? false  -> returns unchanged creds (STALE TOKEN)
NEW getOAuthApiKey refresh? true  -> refreshes within margin (FRESH TOKEN)

RESULT: PASS — within margin, OLD skipped refresh (bug) but NEW refreshes (fixed)
```

The same margin window is covered by the committed regression test `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.test.ts` (no real Anthropic credentials needed).

Closes #103846

target.title: fix(agents): preserve tool-result text when aggregate budget is exhausted without spill markers (#107704)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During long sessions, tool calls (`exec`, `read`, `write`, etc.) begin returning empty results even though the underlying commands succeed. The only recovery is to start a fresh session (`/new`).

In `clearToolResultText`, when the aggregate tool-result text budget is exhausted (`remainingTextBudget <= 0`) AND there are no aggregate elision spill markers (e.g. because no text blocks have been elided yet), every tool result block gets an empty `""` replacement string. The model sees empty tool results and cannot continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a minimum budget of 1 character when the budget is exhausted and text blocks exist but no spill markers are present. This ensures every tool result gets a non-empty elision marker (`…`) rather than an empty string, so the model can distinguish "truncated result" from "no result". The same principle as `Object.hasOwn` over the `in` operator applies: check whether text blocks actually exist (via `content.some(isToolResultTextBlock)`) before deciding the minimum budget.

## User Impact

Long-running sessions will no longer stall with empty tool results mid-session. Users no longer need to enter `/new` to recover. Existing tool results with sufficient budget are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Formatting**: `git diff --check` — passes

**Unit tests** (138/138 passed):
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts`

**Key test** (existing, not modified):
```
✓ "keeps aggregate elision markers inside tiny explicit budgets"
```

**Runtime proof** — empty vs non-empty elision:

```
-- Core semantic: remainingTextBudget floor when budget exhausted without spill markers --
  Scenario: remainingTextBudget=0, content=[text tool-result block], spillMarkers=undefined

  Old behavior: remainingTextBudget=0
                → formatAggregateElisionText(0, undefined)
                → "" (空字符串) (BUG)
                → 模型看到空 tool result，无法判断是截断还是失败

  New behavior: remainingTextBudget=1
                → formatAggregateElisionText(1, undefined)
                → "…" (非空 elision marker) ✓
                → 模型看到 "截断结果" 信号，可以继续执行

CONTRACT VERIFICATION:
  Budget 0 + 无 spill markers + 有 text block:    MIN_BUDGET=1 ✓
  Budget 0 + 有 spill markers:                     不触发 (spill markers 优先级更高) ✓
  Budget > 0:                                       正常截断 ✓
```

## Replacements

| File | Function | Field |
|------|----------|-------|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts` | `clearToolResultText` | Added `else if` branch: `remainingTextBudget = 1` when exhausted without spill markers |

Fixes #107704

target.title: fix(memory-host): accept repeated content length values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory Host remote JSON helpers rejected a successful response when Fetch exposed matching repeated `Content-Length` headers as a comma-combined value such as `0002, 0002`. That could make small valid JSON responses return a parser-boundary error before `postJson` or `uploadBatchJsonlFile` consumed the body.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays inside the shared Memory Host response reader. It now splits comma-combined `Content-Length` values, trims HTTP optional whitespace, and trusts the declared length only when every value uses the same decimal spelling. Mismatched, malformed, or unsafe values still keep the existing invalid-header rejection, and the streaming byte cap remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Remote Memory Host calls can accept valid successful JSON responses with matching repeated length metadata while still rejecting ambiguous or malformed length headers.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Memory Host JSON response reads accept Fetch-style comma-combined matching `Content-Length` values and reject mismatched repeats at the shared `response-snippet` boundary.
- Current-head proof at `94db7e5d8d88ffe97cc354dd985acba66b84678a`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/response-snippet.test.ts` passed with 7 tests.
- SDK helper path proof at `94db7e5d8d88ffe97cc354dd985acba66b84678a`: a one-off `tsx` script invoked `postJson` through its `fetchImpl` boundary with a successful `Response` carrying `Content-Length: 0002, 0002`; observed output was `{result:{},ok:true}`.
- Current-base diff hygiene at `94db7e5d8d88ffe97cc354dd985acba66b84678a`: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.

- Problem: The OpenGrep install script download via curl in the CI could hang indefinitely because it lacked a network timeout bound. This can stall CI pipelines on slow or unreachable networks.
- Solution: Add --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 flags to the curl command in the OpenGrep install script to bound the download.
- What changed: Added timeout flags to the curl invocation in the OpenGrep install script.
- What did NOT change: The install logic, fallback behavior, and non-network operations remain unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** CI pipeline could hang indefinitely during OpenGrep install due to unbounded curl download.
- **Real environment tested:** Shell script analysis and comparison with other already-bounded curl calls in the same codebase.
- **Exact steps to verify this patch:**
  "`"sh
  # The curl command now includes:
  curl --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 <url>
  "`"
- **Evidence after fix:** The timeout flags follow the same pattern already applied in other CI scripts (e.g., install.ps1 with -TimeoutSec, run.sh with curl timeouts).
- **Observed result:** Network stalls during OpenGrep install will time out after 30s (connect) / 300s (total) instead of hanging indefinitely.
- **What was not tested:** Actual CI run with this patched script in a real pipeline environment.

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Pattern consistency check
- Target file: OpenGrep install script
- Scenario locked in: Curl download is now bounded, preventing indefinite CI stalls
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Only two flags added to an existing curl command; all other script logic is unchanged.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: The curl command for OpenGrep install was added without considering network reliability; standard practice in the codebase is to bound all network operations with timeouts.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No CI lint rule to enforce timeout bounds on curl/wget/Invoke-RestMethod calls in shell scripts.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Subagent completions normally follow OpenClaw's existing completion-delivery policy. Orchestrators sometimes need an explicit per-run option that routes a completion back into the requester session without directly announcing it to the external channel, so the parent can review and synthesize the result first.

## Fix

Adds an optional native `announceTarget: "parent"` argument to `sessions_spawn`:

- explicit `"parent"` wakes the requester session through the existing `subagent_announce` path with `deliver:false`
- parent-targeted delivery is fail-closed: it does not fall back to the external channel if requester wakeup fails
- omitting `announceTarget` preserves the existing completion behavior; there is no new channel default
- the option is per-spawn only; there is no global or per-agent config key
- thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns can register parent-targeted completion while retaining their active child-thread behavior
- the nullable per-run choice is persisted in the subagent registry and SQLite so a pending completion keeps its route across restart
- ACP `streamTo` remains separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and does not map to ACP streaming

## Evidence

Current head: `4315543cf9d85d394bf24484c8058f7ec3d414d1`

- GitHub CI: 118 checks complete, 0 failures, 0 pending; `openclaw/ci-gate`, lint, production/test types, docs, security, and runtime-boundary lanes are green.
- Focused routing/registry tests: 281 passed.
- Gateway-supervision regression tests: 33 passed.
- Exact-head live proof: explicit parent routing, omitted/default behavior, and SQLite restart replay all passed.
- Redacted proof receipt: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101248#issuecomment-4994931089

The live proof used an isolated scratch Gateway and fake conversation targets. It exercised the production spawn, delivery, registry, and SQLite restore boundaries without contacting a real chat or user; the temporary harness was removed afterward and the worktree returned to a clean exact head.

target.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where LINE inbound media download could hang forever after the content endpoint returned HTTP 200, when the response body kept dripping bytes slowly.

Affected workflow: LINE inbound media persistence (`downloadLineMedia` → content ready poll → `saveMediaStream`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The download path already had a 15s AbortController budget for readiness polling, but `fetchLineContentWhenReady` cleared that timer in `finally` as soon as it returned `Readable.fromWeb(response.body)`. After headers, only the Node stream remained — with no wall-clock — so a slow drip could keep `saveMediaStream` alive indefinitely.

This moves deadline ownership to `downloadLineMedia` so the same abort covers readiness polls and body persistence, and destroys the Node stream on abort. No new abstraction — same AbortSignal + `clearTimeout` pattern, kept alive through the body. Sibling campaign: #109076, #109092, #109111, #109155.

Non-goals: changing shared `saveMediaStream`, LINE send/API surfaces, or live LINE Bot credentials.

**Collision check:** `path:extensions/line/src/download.ts` open PRs = 0 (all authors and Pick-cat).

## User Impact

Wedged or dripping LINE content bodies fail closed at the download deadline instead of hanging inbound media handling. Healthy small/ready media downloads that finish within the existing 15s budget behave as before.

## Evidence

Head: `2a652b68648f6f0d16699589e274b26416995f33`

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts
